newsitem.title: USA: Cerion sees Q3 loss, lower revenues.
newsitem.headline: Cerion sees Q3 loss, lower revenues.

text.p: Cerion Technologies Inc said on Wednesday it expects to report a net loss of $0.05 to $0.10 a share for the third quarter and anticipates that revenues will be down significantly from a year ago.
In the 1995 third quarter Cerion, which makes precision-machined aluminum disk substrates, earned $854,000, or $0.16 a share.
Cerion said it expects revenues for the third quarter to be below the 1996 second quarter level of $13.4 million.

"Several factors are affecting our third-quarter performance. Previously, we had announced that StorMedia, our second-largest customer, had canceled all outstanding purchase orders with Cerion," David Peterson, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

The loss of this business, combined with lower than anticipated orders from other customers and pricing pressures in the disk drive industry, will cause a substantial revenue shortfall and net loss in the third quarter, he said.

"Results for the fourth quarter will be affected by industry conditions as they continue to develop," Peterson said. "In response to current conditions, we have implemented a temporary two-week shutdown of our manufacturing facility and will take the necessary actions to bring costs in line with current volumes."
He said Cerion will aggressively seek customers to replace the lost sales volume.
The company expects to report third-quarter results during the week of October 14.
